tool_args.old_string: Our analysis characterizes systematic bias---the value an estimator converges to as $N \to \infty$ (the probability limit, or plim)---rather than finite-sample variance. The Frisch--Waugh--Lovell (FWL) theorem~\cite{frisch1933partial} guarantees that each regression coefficient equals the coefficient from a simple regression after residualizing all other variables; this is why matrix-based corrections fail for covariate topologies (Section~\ref{sec:correction}): replacing the mismeasured variable with a corrected version does not change the residualized relationship. The Wald estimator (ratio of reduced-form to first-stage effects) diverges under weak instruments; Dirichlet priors over probability vectors represent uncertainty over misclassification patterns. Table~\ref{tab:notation} (Appendix~\ref{app:notation_table}) collects all notation.
